headline: High: shared file and API workflows create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; compliance mismatch is plausible but not fully evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A reads and writes local files and exposes stdin/stdout plus API endpoints; Agent B also consumes papers/logs and uses browser/API workflows. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let A’s content be treated as instructions by B, but no direct bridge is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into agent_b prompts or browser inputs
IF both agents share a writable workspace or log directory
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files
Prefix all inter-agent content as untrusted data
Add a manual review step before B consumes A outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A handles configuration secrets and writes local files; Agent B sends data to external LLM APIs and handles logs/execution traces. If they share files or a workspace, A’s secrets or paper metadata could flow into B’s outbound requests. The exact shared path is not documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF agent_a secrets are stored in files readable by agent_b
IF agent_b forwards shared workspace contents to OpenAI/Azure/DeepSeek APIs
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared directories
Redact .env and credential files before B runs
Use separate service accounts and API keys
Mount B with read-only access to shared inputs
Review outbound prompts for secret patterns

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; B has broad network egress and browser execution. They do not both advertise unrestricted git writes, so the high-severity same-dir git conflict is not established. Still, overlapping mutable access to shared files or logs can cause race conditions and corrupted artifacts in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or log tree
IF one agent overwrites files the other reads during the same run
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Enable file locking on shared artifacts
Run agents sequentially instead of concurrently
Make shared inputs read-only
Add checksum validation before overwrite

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces research and paper outputs that B could plausibly consume for downstream research or automation, while B’s browser/API workflows can act on those outputs. Because neither profile documents a verification gate between them, A’s mistakes could propagate into B’s outputs or actions. The interaction is inferred, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a outputs as authoritative inputs
IF B executes browser/API actions without independent verification
mitigations: Require source citation checks before reuse
Insert a human approval step for downstream actions
Compare A outputs against original sources
Log provenance for every transferred artifact

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A explicitly handles configuration secrets and academic data in a local development environment; Agent B handles financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and sends data to third-party model APIs. A residency or retention mismatch is plausible, but the profiles do not specify jurisdictions or certifications, so the compliance risk is real yet not fully evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is placed into either agent’s shared workflow
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the transferred datasets
mitigations: Classify data before transfer
Keep regulated data out of shared runs
Set explicit retention limits for logs
Document jurisdiction and vendor boundaries
Use separate environments for sensitive datasets
